display_name: Suheldev of Bahraich & Ghazi Miyan (Salar Masud)
one_line: Twin memory-figures of Bahraich: a local defender-king and a young warrior-saint linked to early Ghaznavid campaigns.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their mid-20s: Suheldev lean and broad-shouldered, Ghazi Miyan slightly slimmer but athletic.
appearance.face: Suheldev has an oval face, wheatish complexion, strong brows, straight nose, trimmed moustache and short beard, with a focused, resolute expression; Ghazi Miyan has a slightly longer face, light-brown complexion, fine straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard, gentle but intense gaze and calm, contemplative smile.
appearance.hair: Suheldev’s black hair is medium-length, straight and tied back in a low warrior’s knot, with a simple dark-brown leather headband; Ghazi Miyan’s black hair is mostly covered by a plain white cloth turban wound close to the head, with a short fringe visible at the forehead.
appearance.costume: Suheldev wears an early-11th-century north Indian warrior’s outfit: a knee-length quilted cotton coat (padded brigandine style) in deep forest green with narrow mustard-yellow piping at the edges, worn over a long-sleeved off-white cotton tunic and dull-red cotton churidar-style trousers; a broad brown leather belt with a simple bronze buckle cinches his waist, from which hangs a small cloth pouch; over one shoulder is a faded indigo cotton sash; on his forearms are brown leather bracers; his feet are in sturdy brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; minimal jewellery: a simple bronze torque necklace and small round bronze studs in the ears. Ghazi Miyan wears modest, shrine-appropriate attire reflecting an early Turkic-Indian warrior-saint: a long, loose, ankle-length cotton robe (qaba-style) in soft sky blue with a slightly darker blue band at the hem and cuffs, over a plain off-white under-tunic; the robe is tied with a narrow dark-brown leather belt; his white, close-wound turban has no ornament; a light olive-green cotton shawl drapes from one shoulder, suggesting both travel and piety; he wears simple dark-brown leather shoes; jewellery is minimal—just a small silver ring on the right hand, echoing a devotional ring, and no other adornment.
appearance.signature: Suheldev carries a single, slightly curved steel sword with a plain iron cross-guard and a dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt, sheathed in a simple brown scabbard; Ghazi Miyan carries a long ash-wood spear with an iron leaf-shaped head, the shaft wrapped with a narrow white cloth band near the grip, held upright like a standard.

ref_desc: A mid-20s Suheldev with wheatish oval face, low black warrior’s knot, forest-green quilted coat over off-white tunic and red trousers, brown belt and shoes, indigo sash and a simple curved sword beside a mid-20s Ghazi Miyan with light-brown face, white turban, sky-blue robe over off-white under-tunic, olive-green shawl, brown shoes and a long ash-wood spear, all in forest green, sky blue, off-white and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of two historically grounded 11th-century Bahraich figures standing side by side: Suheldev and Ghazi Miyan, shown as dignified, modestly dressed warriors whose shared scene hints at later shrine memory rather than a specific battle. Suheldev is a lean, broad-shouldered man in his mid-20s with an oval wheatish face, strong brows, trimmed moustache and short beard, his default expression focused and resolute; his straight black hair is medium-length, tied back in a low warrior’s knot, with a simple dark-brown leather headband. He wears a knee-length quilted cotton coat in deep forest green with narrow mustard-yellow piping, over a long-sleeved off-white cotton tunic and dull-red churidar-style trousers; a broad brown leather belt with a bronze buckle, a small pouch, and a faded indigo cotton sash over one shoulder; brown leather forearm bracers and sturdy brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes, plus a simple bronze torque necklace and small bronze ear studs. His signature weapon is a slightly curved steel sword with a plain iron cross-guard and dark-brown leather-wrapped hilt, in a brown scabbard at his side, held or resting so its full length is visible. Beside him, Ghazi Miyan (Salar Masud) appears as a slightly slimmer but athletic young man in his mid-20s, with a light-brown complexion, slightly longer face, fine straight nose, neat short beard, and a calm, contemplative smile with intense eyes; his black hair is mostly covered by a plain white cloth turban wound close to the head, with a short fringe at the forehead. He wears a modest, ankle-length sky-blue cotton robe with a slightly darker blue band at hem and cuffs, over a plain off-white under-tunic, tied at the waist with a narrow dark-brown leather belt; a light olive-green cotton shawl drapes from one shoulder, and he has simple dark-brown leather shoes and a small silver ring on his right hand. His signature prop is a long ash-wood spear with an iron leaf-shaped head and a narrow white cloth band near the grip, held upright like a standard. Emphasize clean, consistent anime lines, forest green, sky blue, off-white and brown leather as dominant colors, and show them in neutral poses from head to toe so the design can be reused in many panels.
